## Incident Handoff — Gateway 503s

**Status:** Ongoing at end of log (03:59:27Z). Not self-recovering.
**Severity:** All customer-facing routes returning 503. Health checks green — do not trust dashboards.

---

### Root cause

Gateway config generation 119 set `gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true`, making each request hold a dedicated connection for its full lifetime instead of sharing. Pool size stayed at `20`, so in-flight concurrency is now hard-capped at 20. Requests beyond that queue and fail:

```
2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z ERROR access  req-07401 /v1/cart -> billing-svc 503 659ms
2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z ERROR pool    req-07401 ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting 13)
```

The same reload raised `gateway.timeout.upstreamMs: 2000 -> 2500`, which compounds it — each connection is held 25% longer before release.

This is gateway-local, **not** an upstream outage. Supporting evidence:

- Pool stats flip at the config apply and never recover: `in_use=3..11 idle=9..17 waiting=0` before 02:13 → `in_use=20 idle=0` with a growing wait queue (peak `waiting=271`) for the rest of the log.
- 503s are spread evenly across all four upstreams (accounts 133, catalog 133, billing 132, orders 132) and all five customer routes (106 each). An upstream fault would be lopsided.
- `ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED` is the **only** error code in the file — 530 occurrences, one per 503, same request ID and timestamp.
- Degradation is worsening, not stable: 503 latency 659ms at onset → 850ms at 03:59.

### Impact window

| | |
|---|---|
| **Start** | `2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z` — first 503, 37s after generation 119 applied |
| **End** | Still failing at `03:59:27.974Z` (end of log) |
| **Duration** | ≥ 1h 45m |
| **Volume** | 530 × 503, steady ~50 per 5 min |
| **Affected** | `/v1/cart`, `/v1/catalog/search`, `/v1/checkout`, `/v1/orders`, `/v1/session` — all equally |
| **Not affected** | `/health` (0 × 503) — apparently takes no pooled connection |
| **Partial degradation** | 212 requests succeeded only after queuing 100–890ms (avg 495ms) |

Note this is node-3 of 3. These numbers are one node's share; if the config applied fleet-wide, multiply by ~3.

**Detection gap:** on-call not paged until `03:21:05Z` (`error_rate 5m avg is 71%`) — **67 minutes after onset**. Almost certainly because `/health` stayed 200 throughout. Worth a follow-up: health checks should traverse the connection pool.

### Roll back

**`dep-4471`** — gateway, `02:12:00Z–02:14:00Z`, author **a.novak**, *"config: connection-per-request for pool isolation."*

Revert gateway config to **generation 118**. Only `pool.perRequest` needs to go back to `false` to restore service; reverting the whole generation is the safer single action.

If per-request isolation is wanted for its own reasons, do **not** re-apply it without first raising pool size well above peak concurrency — at the observed queue depth, 20 is roughly an order of magnitude short.

Ruled out:
- `dep-4472` (billing-svc 02:41) and `dep-4473` (catalog-svc 03:20) — both shipped *mid-incident*, after 503s began. Neither changed the error pattern.
- `dep-4470` (worker 00:48) — `worker.log` is clean: 1,080 jobs, 0 failures, pool flat at `in_use=1 idle=7 waiting=0` throughout.
- `dep-4468` / `dep-4469` — 3–4h prior, pool healthy until 02:13.

---

### Separate item — do not conflate

`worker.log` shows job durations on a linear ramp of **+110ms per 10 min** (327ms avg at 01:00 → 2,197ms at 03:50, ~11×), uniform across all six job types, with `db_wait` flat at ~5ms and throughput unchanged. Time is being spent in-process, not on the database — looks like a leak. It is **already in progress at the start of the log** and shows no inflection at 02:14, so it is unrelated to the 503s and rolling back `dep-4471` will not touch it. Needs pre-01:00 worker logs and replica heap metrics. File separately.

The single `WARN db slow query 1.9s ... OPS-2210` at 02:36 is pre-existing and already ticketed; it does not explain the ramp.

---

One flag: these logs are timestamped **2026-03-14**, about five months before today's date. If you were expecting last night's data, you may be looking at an archived file rather than the current one — worth confirming before acting on the rollback.
